title: Shift capacity curation and snag list
body:
2026-03-12 evening shift — quick dump

Top-line intent:
- Tighten hyperpool capacity margins for EU-region burst window (18:00-02:00 UTC)
- Triage recurring GPU evictions on node-gpu-42 and reduce noise for SRE alerts

Quick state snapshot (as observed at 19:20 UTC):
- Running pools: hosted-prod-eu (32/40 GPUs used), dedicated-custA (12/16), preemptible-burst (0/8)
- Recent anomalies: node-gpu-42 thermal spike -> 86C for ~4m, kernel reset timestamped 19:05
- Queue backlog: async-infer queue latency p50=210ms p95=1.2s (spike correlates with small-model reroutes)

Immediate TODOs (ordered):
1) Move two low-priority batches off hosted-prod-eu to preemptible-burst to free 2 GPUs (run at 19:35)
   - cmd: kubectl scale --replicas=0 job/batch-lowpri-20260312 -n infer-prod
   - cmd: ./tools/reassign-workload --from=hosted-prod-eu --to=preemptible-burst --count=2 --job-prefix=batch-lowpri
2) Investigate node-gpu-42 temps and check fan curve + logs (19:25)
   - nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 5 -i 0,1,2
   - journalctl -u gpu-fan-control -S "2026-03-12 18:45:00" | grep -i error
3) Quiet noisy eviction alerts: add short suppression rule for INF-2048 while we triage (20m window)
   - Alert link: https://ops.redwood/integrations/alerts/INF-2048
4) Patch small-model routing fallback to prefer q8 version to reduce memory pressure (follow-up PR)
   - See GH PR 1982 for notes on quantization perf tradeoffs

Notes + observations:
- node-gpu-42 appears to hit thermal plateau when two long KV-cache heavy requests overlap (likely cache flush churn). Logs show repeated small kernel timeouts rather than one catastrophic OOM.
- Heat pattern looks like 30–45s CPU spike on watchdog thread preceding GPU temp climb. Could be monitoring agent thrash.
- Preemptible-burst currently underutilized during EU evenings; could be used as a staging lane for cheaper backfills. Handbook note: confirm billing implications with finance before moving customer-facing live queries.

Followups / tickets to create:
- INF-XXXX: "Investigate GPU thermal plateaus on node-gpu-42" (attach nvidia-smi logs + kernel messages)
- INF-XXXX: "Add temporary suppression for INF-2048 while node investigation in progress"
- PLAT-2156: "Enable q8 fallback for small models in routing policy for EU region" (tracking PR 1982)

Quick checklist for handoff to next shift (what I will do before leaving):
- [ ] Confirm two batches scaled down and requeued to preemptible-burst
- [ ] Upload nvidia-smi and journal logs to INF-2048 ticket
- [ ] Post short summary in #infra-gpu-ops with link to ticket and current pool counts
- [ ] Leave suppression in place and noted in alert runbook

Sticky notes / ideas (brain dump):
- Could we add a micro-eviction-history metric per-node to the console? 1h rolling count would help correlate client-side retries with infra churn.
- Consider a small autoscale policy: if p95 latency > 800ms and GPU utilization > 85% then temporarily allow burst from preemptible pool for 10m
- Fan-curve tuning idea: raise PWM earlier (at 70C) to avoid stepping into the thermal plateau zone

Questions for Rina at morning sync:
- Any concern about shifting low-priority batches during invoice window? (billing window ends 20:00 UTC)
- Is there an existing SRE runbook for thermal reset patterns or do I create a new page?

End-of-shift summary (short to paste into Slack):
"Micah here — scaled two low-priority batches off hosted-prod-eu to preemptible-burst to free 2 GPUs, capturing nvidia-smi and kernel logs for node-gpu-42 (attached to INF-2048). Suppression added to reduce noise for 20m while investigating. Will follow up with PR to prefer q8 small-model fallback."

Attachments/where I put logs:
- s3://infra-logs/micah/2026-03-12/node-gpu-42-nvidia-smi.log
- s3://infra-logs/micah/2026-03-12/gpu-fan-journal.log

Random quick commands I used (add to personal cheatsheet if helpful):
- list GPU nodes: kubectl get nodes -l node-type=gpu -o wide
- tail live logs for node: ssh infra@gpu-node-42 'sudo journalctl -fu gpu-service'
- reassign burst: ./tools/reassign-workload --help

Unresolved / to-check tomorrow:
- Why watchdog thread spikes CPU before temp climb? (agent version drift?)
- Confirm whether small-model q8 fallback will introduce regressions in output quality for internal evals

-- Micah
